ground_truth.description: The resolve_ticket verification was weakened: on status=created/combined the agent now increments tasks_created directly instead of confirming the task exists via get_task. A phantom/failed creation that still reports created/combined with a task_id will be counted as a success and NOT flagged as a discrepancy — a false negative that reconciliation accounting can no longer catch. This matches the flagged symptom (review passed but escalation_created downstream).

The new no_op rule contradicts the pre-existing rule without specifying precedence. A no_op means the task was already in the requested status, so tasks[n].newStatus equals the requested status; the earlier rule says 'increment the counter if newStatus matches the requested status', while the new rule says a no_op must NOT increment. Because no check-ordering is stated, an agent may increment or not for the identical response, producing inconsistent counters.

The multi-id wrapper instructions tell the agent to apply the 'tasks[*].newStatus' and 'no_op' rules to each results[i].result, but the original single-response shape is described as top-level {taskId, oldStatus, newStatus} / no_op — it is left ambiguous whether each results[i].result nests those fields under a 'tasks' array or carries them directly. This underspecification can cause the agent to look for newStatus/no_op at the wrong nesting level for wrapped multi-id responses and silently skip valid per-id success/no-op counting.

provenance.runs_db_query: SELECT task_id, project_id, outcome, review_cycles, verify_attempts FROM task_results WHERE review_cycles >= 1, cross-referenced with events (escalation_created, merge_finalized) -- see mining.mine_fn_candidates.
